subject: china-studies
title: Urbanisation: One Chinese City Changes Across the Decades Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says a Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - photographs prove the city replaced the farmland in one step
Urbanisation is gradual and driven by people moving in: factories and housing are built on farmland at the edge stage by stage, districts spread outward, and the urban share climbs at every stage.
The city became urban when its boundary was redrawn, before anything was built
The farmland is still all there - the city was built somewhere else

questions.misconception: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: A Chinese city becomes urban in one sudden leap, because its farmland is replaced by built-up districts all at once. Reteach point: Urbanisation is gradual and driven by people moving in: factories and the first housing blocks are built on farmland at the edge as migrants arrive for jobs, the built-up districts then spread outward stage by stage, and the urban population share climbs - and the rural share falls - at every stage until the city is mostly built-up.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, give the urban share at the first and final stages and say what drives the climb between them.
questions.answer: The urban share climbs from 15 of every 100 people at the first stage to 85 at the final stage, driven by people moving in for factory jobs as housing and districts are built stage by stage.
questions.feedback: A strong answer pairs the two end shares with the driver: people moving in, not a single building step.

questions.prompt: In the animation, the farmland shrinks to a strip in the west when:

choices.text: The city is replaced in one sudden leap
The built-up districts spread outward from the core and the factories in stage 3
The small town is first built where the roads cross
The rural share climbs back above the urban share

questions.feedback: Scene 3 shows the districts spreading outward and the farmland shrinking to a western strip as the urban share reaches 62.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, name the four stages the city passes through in order.
questions.answer: Farmland and a small town, then factories and first housing at the edge, then built-up districts spreading outward, then a mostly built-up city reached in stages.
questions.feedback: A strong answer keeps the stages in order - each one builds on the last, which is exactly what the sudden-leap claim misses.
